I93.title: Verification gate v2: generic name-collision detection (remove per-company rules) and a harder unseen-company benchmark
I93.why: Found while re-checking I06 (claude-f41b, 2026-10-27). intel/verify.py KNOWN_COLLISION_RULES (lines 155-214) is a per-brand table keyed on asco, emmegi, pomini, corrada: the golden company and the I03 dev/hold-out companies, with exception patterns holding the golden company's real owners (mott, idex, binasco). It is the only collision detector (single call site, line 387), so it breaks roadmap rule 'never hard-code the golden company, its names or pages' and contaminates the Pomini and Emmegi hold-outs. It does not generalise: probe with the same namesake shape (page 'Emerson {BRAND} solenoid valves ... distributor in Milano', company city Milano) gives ASCO rejected/collision, but an unseen brand (ZETA FILTRI) verified=True with no collision. The 24-case benchmark (precision 1.0) does not show generalisation: TN01-TN05 pages contain no discriminator, so the generic no-discriminator rule rejects them even without the table; no case has a namesake page that also mentions the company's city or a known person. Do: replace the table with generic detection from the page and search results themselves (roadmap I06: second entity with the same brand token but a different legal form, city, domain or group name; page about a larger/different entity that only incidentally mentions the discriminator; brand token that is a common surname or common word; page host belongs to another company); keep any lexical hints in a config file as data with NO company names; rebuild the benchmark with at least 20 hard negatives on companies not named in the code, including namesake pages that contain one discriminator, and report precision and recall on a split the author did not tune on. Accept: grep of intel/ for asco|emmegi|pomini|corrada|mott|idex finds no rule; precision >= 0.95 on the new hard set; the old 24 cases still pass.

That breaks roadmap rule 6 (do not game the benchmark), so the I14 golden score is not evidence the collector works on unseen companies. Also found: it never uses ctx.search (I05) or intel.verify (I06, a name-only entity check lets same-brand firms through); a parent-company CEO is stored under people.managing_director; an audit firm is stored as people.board_member; the registry roster read swallows all errors; scripts/intel_run.py gives collectors no search client. Rework: remove all company-specific data, discover pages with the I05 query pack and verify with I06, fix the misclassifications, wire search into intel_run.py (additive), re-score honestly.

I100.title: Verifier: compound-entity detector reads a line break as a space (headline + body creates a false namesake)
I100.why: Found while building I95 on the I93 verifier. intel/verify.py _compound_entity_hits() matches '{Capitalized} {brand}' with \s+, which spans a line break, so a page whose headline ends in a capitalised word and whose next line starts with the company name is read as a foreign compound entity and the fact is rejected as a name collision. Minimal repro: company legal name 'MECCANICA BRAMBILLA S.R.L.' (invented), page text 'Meccanica Brambilla entra nel gruppo Orion<newline>Meccanica Brambilla di Lecco ha annunciato ...' without the legal form on the page: verify() returns 'Name-collision ... (Orion<newline>Meccanica)'. Headline-then-body is the normal shape of extracted press text, so this costs recall on ordinary pages (it rejects, so it is the safe direction, but a collector built on verify() silently loses true facts). Fix: do not let a compound cross a newline or sentence end (use [^\S\n]+ between the two tokens, and treat . ! ? : as a boundary), add the repro as a regression test. Describe the ticket under ### I97 in docs/INTEL_ROADMAP.md on your branch.

I104.title: Search layer reliability: silent provider failures, Google News redirect links, GDELT throttling, DuckDuckGo unreachable
I104.why: Probed 2026-10-27 from the dev machine with the layer's own User-Agent: DuckDuckGo html and root time out at TCP connect (DNS resolves); Google News RSS answers 200 but every link is an encoded news.google.com/rss/articles redirect, so fetching it yields no article; GDELT answers 429 'one request every 5 seconds' as plain text and resp.json() fails. intel/search.py swallows every provider error and returns [], so a block, a throttle and a true 'no results' look identical, and collectors (I14, I13) report absence-looking empties. Needed: per-provider health and the reason in the result (never [] for an error), a shared throttle and back-off for GDELT across processes, publisher-URL resolution for Google News items (or use the title/source and search again), and at least one provider that works reliably without spoofing a browser (decision G1 recommends one keyed provider; do not circumvent bot checks). Acceptance: an offline test per failure mode, and a live ASCO ownership pack returning pages that mention the owner, with the providers that failed named in the output.
